findings.title: Dense padding can exceed the architecture’s CPU-scale memory budget
findings.description: The padded representation allocates `n_active × max_neighbors` entries, and the design explicitly includes the all-same-cluster case where `max_neighbors` can approach the population size. The 80KB estimate is for 100 agents; at 10,000 densely clustered agents, the neighbor indices and mask alone would use roughly 900MB, before the gathered position/velocity arrays and temporary reductions. That risks making the force path unusable at the architecture’s tens-of-thousands CPU scale. Bound the dense working set—for example, by processing in chunks—or choose a representation that does not require materializing population-wide padded gathers.

findings.title: Per-agent profile lookup still uses Python iteration inside force calls
findings.description: The proposed weight construction uses a Python list comprehension over agents for each force call. That conflicts with the slice’s requirement of no Python-level per-agent loops in `BulkForce.__call__` and the architecture’s vectorized hot-loop principle. Build profile-field arrays indexed by `profile_indices`, or otherwise arrange the lookup so force calls use array operations rather than iterating over agents in Python.

findings.title: The new neighbor interface cannot represent aggregate neighbors
findings.description: `NeighborData` stores only integer indices, and the force pattern gathers position and velocity directly from individual-agent state arrays. It cannot represent the aggregate neighbor data the architecture describes (such as centroid, heading, dispersion, and population count). The architecture requires the force/spatial-query interfaces to accommodate heterogeneous neighbors from the start. This slice need not implement aggregates, but it should preserve a representation or extension point that can carry them without a breaking interface change.

findings.title: Verification does not cover the architecture’s stated scale target
findings.description: The architecture calls for full-fidelity evaluation of tens of thousands of agents on a single CPU. The slice’s live verification targets 100 agents and a 50ms tick budget; it does not restate or validate the tens-of-thousands CPU target for this hot path. Add a performance acceptance criterion at the architecture’s stated scale, with a specific tick-time or throughput target.
